answer: A single sparrow of a bot is harmless; the danger is the flock, so the network makes attesters stake something real. Every countersignature is a bond: if a later audit proves the transaction you vouched for was junk, the bond burns and your weight resets. Because a mirror of identical accounts would simply vouch for itself, seat draws are weighted by reciprocity with strangers rather than by who you already know. That stretches the payoff horizon: faking one epoch is cheap, but holding weight across many while bonding every signature costs more than honest work returns.
